title: Everything Went Dark, No Pain

patient.name: Mr Yeo Kah Wai
patient.presenting_complaint: Sudden, painless loss of vision in the right eye about 40 minutes ago

history.hpc: Mr Yeo walks up to the counter looking worried. He says: 'Suddenly my right eye cannot see, like curtain come down, but no pain at all.' It happened about 40 minutes ago and has not improved. Sudden painless loss of vision is a red flag — central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) with VA <6/60 is a Category 1 emergency where time is critical.
history.social_hx: Retired. Smoker. Came in by himself.

iop.right: to be checked but must not delay escalation

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Quiet, white eye (no redness) — typical of painless vision loss

investigations.front_line_triage: Recognise sudden painless severe vision loss as a Category 1 emergency (CRAO with VA <6/60 — within 10 minutes). Check VA quickly, flag the vascular risk factors (hypertension, AF, smoking), and escalate to the doctor immediately. Do not place this patient in a routine queue.
investigations.va_distance: RE markedly reduced (CF or worse), LE 6/9.

diagnosis: Sudden painless severe loss of vision, suspicious of central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) — a time-critical Category 1 emergency. The PSA competency is recognising the red flag, triaging it as Category 1, and escalating immediately rather than booking a routine slot.

immediate: Recognise sudden painless vision loss as a major red flag, not a routine complaint
Triage as Category 1 (CRAO with VA <6/60 — see doctor within 10 minutes)
Quickly check VA in both eyes without delaying escalation
Alert the doctor immediately and do not leave the patient waiting in a routine queue
Note the time of onset and vascular risk factors (hypertension, AF, smoking) for the doctor
Document the presenting complaint, onset time, VA, and the triage category
follow_up: Doctor to assess urgently and manage as indicated
Record the triage outcome on the SNEC triage form (same-day/urgent)
Ensure the patient is escorted to the assessment area promptly
patient_education: Reassure him calmly that he is being seen urgently because this is time-sensitive
Ask him not to leave and to tell staff if anything changes
Avoid giving a diagnosis or prognosis — defer to the doctor
Explain the doctor will examine him very soon

key_points: Establishes the sudden, painless nature and time of onset
Identifies the absence of pain/redness as fitting painless vision loss
Notes vascular risk factors (hypertension, AF, smoking)
Gathers essentials quickly without delaying escalation
Checks VA in both eyes promptly
Recognises VA <6/60 with sudden painless loss as Category 1
Does not delay escalation to perform extra tests
Documents onset time, VA, and triage category
Recognises sudden painless vision loss as a red flag (possible CRAO)
Understands the time-critical nature of the presentation
Knows diagnosis/management is the doctor's role
Escalates to the doctor immediately and avoids a routine queue
Records the triage category and onset time on the triage form
Reassures the patient and keeps him in the assessment area
